cards.name: Tangela
cards.description: Hidden beneath a tangle of vines that grows nonstop even if the vines are torn off, this Pokémon's true appearance remains a mystery.

cards.name: Tangrowth
cards.description: Tangrowth has two arms that it can extend as it pleases. Recent research has shown that these arms are, in fact, bundles of vines.

cards.name: Pinsir
cards.description: These Pokémon judge one another based on pincers. Thicker, more impressive pincers make for more popularity with the opposite gender.

cards.name: Spinarak
cards.description: Some fishers weave its sturdy thread into nets to catch fish Pokémon.

cards.name: Ariados
cards.description: It wanders in search of food after darkness falls, never nesting in a specific place.

cards.name: Sunkern
cards.description: It is very weak. Its only means of defense is to shake its leaves desperately at its attacker.

cards.name: Sunflora
cards.description: Since it converts sunlight into energy, it is always looking in the direction of the sun.

cards.name: Heracross
cards.description: With its herculean powers, it can easily throw around an object that is 100 times its own weight.

cards.name: Volbeat
cards.description: It flashes the light on its rear to communicate with other Volbeat. It loves the sweet aroma given off by Illumise.

cards.name: Illumise
cards.description: It guides Volbeat to draw signs in the night sky. There are scholars who research the meaning of these signs.

cards.name: Leafeon
cards.description: The younger they are, the more they smell like fresh grass. With age, their fragrance takes on the odor of fallen leaves.

cards.name: Phantump
cards.description: This Pokémon came to be when the spirit of a deceased child possessed a tree stump. It now wanders the forest searching for friends.

cards.name: Trevenant
cards.description: Trevenant is very kind to Pokémon living in the forest. It doesn't even care if these Pokémon take up residence in the greenery on its head.

cards.name: Grookey
cards.description: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.

cards.name: Thwackey
cards.description: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.

cards.name: Rillaboom
cards.description: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.

cards.name: Applin
cards.description: Applin lives inside an apple. When an Applin is separated from its apple, its body loses moisture and the Pokémon grows weak.

cards.name: Dipplin
cards.description: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

cards.name: Iron Leaves
cards.description: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.

cards.name: Poltchageist
cards.description: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

cards.name: Poltchageist
cards.description: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

cards.name: Sinistcha
cards.description: It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset.

cards.name: Teal Mask Ogerpon
cards.description: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

cards.name: Vulpix
cards.description: As its body grows larger, its six warm tails become more beautiful, with a more luxurious coat of fur.

cards.name: Ninetales
cards.description: It has nine long tails and fur that gleams gold. It is said to live for 1,000 years.

cards.name: Slugma
cards.description: It's said that in ancient times, when volcanoes were more active, there were many more Slugma than there are now.

cards.name: Torkoal
cards.description: Coal is the source of Torkoal's energy. Large amounts of coal can be found in the mountains where they live.

cards.name: Chimchar
cards.description: Its fiery rear end is fueled by gas made in its belly. Even rain can't extinguish the fire.

cards.name: Monferno
cards.description: It skillfully controls the intensity of the fire on its tail to keep its foes at an ideal distance.

cards.name: Infernape
cards.description: Its crown of fire is indicative of its fiery nature. It is beaten by none in terms of quickness.

cards.name: Darumaka
cards.description: It derives its power from fire burning inside its body. If the fire dwindles, this Pokémon will immediately fall asleep.

cards.name: Darmanitan
cards.description: The thick arms of this hot-blooded Pokémon can deliver punches capable of obliterating a dump truck.

cards.name: Litwick
cards.description: While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life-force of any who follow it.

cards.name: Lampent
cards.description: The spirits it absorbs fuel its baleful fire. It hangs around hospitals waiting for people to pass on.

cards.name: Chandelure
cards.description: It absorbs spirits, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.

cards.name: Chi-Yu
cards.description: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.

cards.name: Poliwag
cards.description: Its legs are newly grown, and it can't walk very well. It seems to prefer swimming through the water instead.

cards.name: Poliwhirl
cards.description: Its skin is moist all over its body. The skin on its belly spiral also feels smooth.

cards.name: Poliwrath
cards.description: It can use its well-developed arms and legs to run on the surface of the water for a split second.

cards.name: Goldeen
cards.description: Its dorsal, pectoral, and tail fins wave elegantly in water. That is why it is known as the Water Dancer.

cards.name: Seaking
cards.description: In autumn, its body becomes more fatty in preparing to propose to a mate. It takes on beautiful colors.

cards.name: Jynx
cards.description: In certain parts of Galar, Jynx was once feared and worshiped as the Queen of Ice.

cards.name: Corphish
cards.description: It can live in impure water, where it doesn't need to compete with other water Pokémon for food, so its numbers have steadily increased.

cards.name: Crawdaunt
cards.description: A rough customer that wildly flails its giant claws. It is said to be extremely hard to raise.

cards.name: Feebas
cards.description: It is the shabbiest Pokémon of all. It forms schools and lives at the bottom of rivers that teem with plant life.

cards.name: Milotic
cards.description: It lives at the bottom of clear lakes. In times of war, it shows itself, which soothes people's minds and hearts.

cards.name: Snorunt
cards.description: It is said that a home visited by a Snorunt will prosper. It can withstand cold of −150 degrees Fahrenheit.

cards.name: Glalie
cards.description: It prevents prey from escaping by instantaneously freezing moisture in the air.

cards.name: Froslass
cards.description: It freezes prey by blowing its −58 degree Fahrenheit breath. It is said to then secretly display its prey.

cards.name: Glaceon
cards.description: It lowers its body heat to freeze its fur. The hairs then become like needles it can fire.

cards.name: Phione
cards.description: When the water warms, they inflate the flotation sac on their heads and drift languidly on the sea in packs.

cards.name: Froakie
cards.description: It secretes flexible bubbles from its chest and back. The bubbles reduce the damage it would otherwise take when attacked.

cards.name: Frogadier
cards.description: It can throw bubble-covered pebbles with precise control, hitting empty cans up to a hundred feet away.

cards.name: Cramorant
cards.description: It's an incredibly poor learner because it uses the bare minimum amount of energy for its brain. It focuses on battling instead.

cards.name: Finizen
cards.description: Its water ring is made from seawater mixed with a sticky fluid that Finizen secretes from its blowhole.

cards.name: Palafin
cards.description: Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen's, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up.

cards.name: Iron Bundle
cards.description: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.

cards.name: Walking Wake
cards.description: This ferocious creature is shrouded in mystery. It's named after an aquatic monster mentioned in an old expedition journal.

cards.name: Zapdos
cards.description: This Pokémon has complete control over electricity. There are tales of Zapdos nesting in the dark depths of pitch-black thunderclouds.

cards.name: Shinx
cards.description: The extension and contraction of its muscles generates electricity. Its fur glows when it's in trouble.

cards.name: Luxio
cards.description: By gathering their tails together, they collectively generate powerful electricity from their claws.

cards.name: Emolga
cards.description: As Emolga flutters through the air, it crackles with electricity. This Pokémon is cute, but it can cause a lot of trouble.

cards.name: Helioptile
cards.description: When spread, the frills on its head act like solar panels, generating the power behind this Pokémon's electric moves.

cards.name: Heliolisk
cards.description: A now-vanished desert culture treasured these Pokémon. Appropriately, when Heliolisk came to the Galar region, treasure came with them.

cards.name: Morpeko
cards.description: It has a small stomach. If it isn't constantly eating the seeds it keeps in its pockets, it will get hungry immediately.

cards.name: Tadbulb
cards.description: It floats using the electricity stored in its body. When thunderclouds are around, Tadbulb will float higher off the ground.

cards.name: Bellibolt
cards.description: What appear to be eyeballs are actually organs for discharging the electricity generated by Bellibolt's belly-button dynamo.

cards.name: Wattrel
cards.description: These Pokémon make their nests on coastal cliffs. The nests have a strange, crackling texture, and they're a popular delicacy.

cards.name: Kilowattrel
cards.description: It uses its throat sac to store electricity generated by its wings. There's hardly any oil in its feathers, so it is a poor swimmer.

cards.name: Clefairy
cards.description: On nights with a full moon, they gather together and dance. The surrounding area is enveloped in an abnormal magnetic field.

cards.name: Clefable
cards.description: It has an acute sense of hearing. It can easily hear a pin being dropped nearly 1,100 yards away.

cards.name: Abra
cards.description: This Pokémon uses its psychic powers while it sleeps. The contents of Abra's dreams affect the powers that the Pokémon wields.

cards.name: Kadabra
cards.description: Using its psychic power, Kadabra levitates as it sleeps. It uses its springy tail as a pillow.

cards.name: Alakazam
cards.description: It has an incredibly high level of intelligence. Some say that Alakazam remembers everything that ever happens to it, from birth till death.

cards.name: Girafarig
cards.description: Girafarig's tail has a small head. It instinctively bites at any foe that approaches the Pokémon from behind.

cards.name: Farigiraf
cards.description: The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.

cards.name: Chimecho
cards.description: Its cries echo inside its hollow body to emerge as beautiful notes for startling and repelling foes.

cards.name: Flabébé
cards.description: This Flabébé rides a red flower. Immediately after birth, this Pokémon begins flying around in search of a flower it likes.

cards.name: Floette
cards.description: This Pokémon uses red wavelengths of light to pour its own energy into flowers and draw forth their latent potential.

cards.name: Florges
cards.description: They say that flower gardens created by Florges are constantly showered with a power that can heal both body and spirit.

cards.name: Swirlix
cards.description: It eats its own weight in sugar every day. If it doesn't get enough sugar, it becomes incredibly grumpy.

cards.name: Slurpuff
cards.description: By taking in a person's scent, it can sniff out their mental and physical condition. It's hoped that this skill will have many medical applications.

cards.name: Sandygast
cards.description: It flings sand into the eyes of its prey and tries to close in on them while they're blinded, but since Sandygast is so slow, the prey tends to escape.

cards.name: Palossand
cards.description: From the hollows in its arms, it fires the bones of its victims, which are all dried up after being drained of their vitality.

cards.name: Enamorus
cards.description: When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.

cards.name: Munkidori
cards.description: Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness.

cards.name: Fezandipiti
cards.description: Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.

cards.name: Sandshrew
cards.description: No matter how high a place it falls from, this Pokémon can save itself by rolling into a ball and bouncing.

cards.name: Sandslash
cards.description: The spikes on its body are made up of its hardened hide. It rolls up and attacks foes with its spikes.

cards.name: Hisuian Growlithe
cards.description: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.

cards.name: Hisuian Arcanine
cards.description: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.

cards.name: Nosepass
cards.description: When endangered, it may protect itself by increasing its magnetism and drawing nearby iron objects to its body.

cards.name: Probopass
cards.description: Probopass radiates such a powerful magnetic field that nearby electrical appliances are rendered useless while it's around.

cards.name: Timburr
cards.description: It fights by swinging a piece of lumber around. It is close to evolving when it can handle heavy lumber without difficulty.

cards.name: Gurdurr
cards.description: This Pokémon is so muscular and strongly built that even a group of wrestlers could not make it budge an inch.

cards.name: Conkeldurr
cards.description: Rather than rely on their strength, they master moves that make good use of centrifugal force to swing around concrete.

cards.name: Hawlucha
cards.description: Hawlucha live quietly without flocking together. They fight constantly with their natural enemies: noisy groups of Primeape.

cards.name: Glimmet
cards.description: Glimmet's toxic mineral crystals look just like flower petals. This Pokémon scatters poisonous powder like pollen to protect itself.

cards.name: Glimmora
cards.description: Glimmora's petals are made of crystallized poison energy. It has recently become evident that these petals resemble Tera Jewels.

cards.name: Ting-Lu
cards.description: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.

cards.name: Okidogi
cards.description: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.

cards.name: Poochyena
cards.description: Poochyena pursue their prey in packs. Once the prey is exhausted, the pack finishes it off. But sometimes the prey retaliates, and the pack flees.

cards.name: Mightyena
cards.description: Once it's caught the scent of faraway prey, the leader gives a signal, and the whole pack moves out.

cards.name: Venipede
cards.description: Venipede and Sizzlipede are similar species, but when the two meet, a huge fight ensues.

cards.name: Whirlipede
cards.description: This Pokémon spins itself rapidly and charges into its opponents. Its top speed is just over 60 mph.

cards.name: Scolipede
cards.description: Scolipede latches on to its prey with the claws on its neck before slamming them into the ground and jabbing them with its claws' toxic spikes.

cards.name: Brute Bonnet
cards.description: It is possible that the creature listed as Brute Bonnet in a certain book could actually be this Pokémon.

cards.name: Skarmory
cards.description: People fashion swords from Skarmory's shed feathers, so this Pokémon is a popular element in heraldic designs.

cards.name: Aron
cards.description: It eats iron ore—and sometimes railroad tracks— to build up the steel armor that protects its body.

cards.name: Lairon
cards.description: Lairon live in mountains brimming with spring water and iron ore, so these Pokémon often came into conflict with humans in the past.

cards.name: Aggron
cards.description: Aggron has a horn sharp enough to perforate thick iron sheets. It brings down its opponents by ramming into them horn first.

cards.name: Heatran
cards.description: It dwells in volcanic caves. It digs in with its cross-shaped feet to crawl on ceilings and walls.

cards.name: Varoom
cards.description: The steel section is Varoom's actual body. This Pokémon clings to rocks and converts the minerals within into energy to fuel its activities.

cards.name: Revavroom
cards.description: Revavroom viciously threatens others with the sound of its exhaust. It sticks its tongue out from its cylindrical mouth and sprays toxic fluids.

cards.name: Applin
cards.description: Applin lives inside an apple. When an Applin is separated from its apple, its body loses moisture and the Pokémon grows weak.

cards.name: Dipplin
cards.description: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

cards.name: Dreepy
cards.description: It has a habit of biting at Clauncher even though it doesn't feed on them. This is said to be vestigial behavior from when Dreepy was alive.

cards.name: Drakloak
cards.description: This Pokémon stores up energy in its lungs, then shoots it out. It takes care of Dreepy and battles alongside them until they're all grown up.

cards.name: Tatsugiri
cards.description: Tatsugiri is an extremely cunning Pokémon. It feigns weakness to lure in prey, then orders its partner to attack.

cards.name: Farfetch'd
cards.description: The stalk this Pokémon carries in its wings serves as a sword to cut down opponents. In a dire situation, the stalk can also serve as food.

cards.name: Chansey
cards.description: It walks carefully to prevent its egg from breaking. However, it is extremely fast at running away.

cards.name: Eevee
cards.description: Its genetic code is irregular. It may mutate if it is exposed to radiation from element stones.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.description: Its stomach's digestive juices can dissolve any kind of poison. Eating things off the ground doesn't bother it at all.

cards.name: Aipom
cards.description: Its tail moves with greater dexterity than its hands. Making deft use of this tail, Aipom lives high among the treetops.

cards.name: Ambipom
cards.description: Split into two, the tails are so adept at handling and doing things that Ambipom rarely uses its hands.

cards.name: Ducklett
cards.description: It strengthens its body by diving into the depths of ponds, swimming around while looking for bog moss to eat.

cards.name: Swanna
cards.description: It's said that many artists have taken inspiration from the sight of a Swanna performing a beautiful dance in the light of dawn.

cards.name: Pinsir
cards.description: These Pokémon judge one another based on pincers. Thicker, more impressive pincers make for more popularity with the opposite gender.

cards.name: Sunflora
cards.description: Since it converts sunlight into energy, it is always looking in the direction of the sun.
